Boxoffy Hype Index · Global Preview · Brand New Day · Jul 31, 2026

Spider-Man is about to do the one thing No Way Home couldn't.

Release in China. That single fact is the difference between a billion-dollar hit and a run at the $2 billion club — and it's the part most of the $700M-opening headlines are skipping. The Boxoffy Hype Index, the premium-screen map, and an honest BCM call on whether Spidey beats his own record.

Share WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram

Next Thursday, an Amazon Prime login gets me into a Spider-Man movie two days before most of America. Next Friday, that movie opens almost everywhere at once. And somewhere in the noise between now and then, one very simple fact keeps getting buried under a pile of increasingly wild numbers.

The fact is this: No Way Home was banned in China and still made $1.9 billion. Brand New Day isn't banned. It opens there. Once you're holding that one detail, most of what you'll read this week starts to look either overheated or beside the point.

Because the headlines have gone somewhere strange. A $700 million global opening. Two-and-a-half billion lifetime. Bigger than Avengers: Doomsday. Those are real posts from real accounts, and they're running well ahead of what the tracking actually says. The trades have this opening near $550 million worldwide — enormous, a hair under No Way Home, and nowhere close to $700M. So the good question isn't "how do we get to $2.5 billion." It's quieter: what happens when the biggest Spider-Man brand in the world finally gets back the one market it was shut out of last time?

That's the piece worth writing. Not the ceiling-chasing, but the China swing, the strange premium-screen map where America loses IMAX and India keeps it, and an honest read on whether Peter Parker can out-earn his own record without the trick — three Spider-Men in one frame — that made the record possible. Here's how it actually stacks up.

The China factor nobody's putting in the headline.

The fact that reframes the whole projection

No Way Home never released in China. It was blocked over a Statue of Liberty sequence in its third act, and still did $1.9 billion worldwide. Brand New Day is releasing in China — and it lands as the most anticipated comic-book film there since Far From Home in 2019.

Sit with that for a second. No Way Home built $1.9 billion with the entire Chinese market switched off. Brand New Day gets that market switched back on, in a year when Chinese survey data ranks it the most anticipated July release in the country, and tracking floats it as maybe the first comic-book film to clear $100 million there since Far From Home, and the first Hollywood live-action film to open to $100 million in China since Avatar: The Way of Water. That is the whole bull case, sitting in one variable. Strip away the noise and every "can it hit $2 billion" headline is asking the same small question: how big is China? The domestic record and the presales are roughly No Way Home-shaped. China is the only part that is genuinely new, so it is the only part worth arguing about.

The premium-screen map.

The IMAX situation is the most misreported thing about this release. It's not "no IMAX." It's a different answer in every market.

MarketIMAX opening wknd?WhyEffect
United StatesNoNolan's Odyssey holds IMAX through ~Aug 14leans on ScreenX / 4DX / D-Box instead
IndiaYesIMAX + regional-language versions from Jul 30premium pricing lifts the India number
ChinaAfter ~2 wksIMAX exclusivity secured post-delayfront-half without, back-half with

So here is the honest version. Brand New Day loses its biggest premium-format market, US IMAX, for opening weekend, keeps it in India, and gets China's on a two-week delay. And it is still tracking to around $550 million globally. Think about what that means: the film is leaving premium money on the table at home and posting the best presales in five years anyway. The IMAX handicap does not shrink the number so much as make it look sturdier. This is demand that does not need the format crutch.

Every rung goes up: $880M, $1.13B, $1.9B. But Brand New Day does not have what made that last jump happen, the once-in-forever sight of three Spider-Men sharing a frame. That is the honest ceiling on it. What it has instead is the market No Way Home was denied. So forget out-hyping No Way Home; the real question is whether a fresh Chinese run can stand in for a nostalgia supernova. That is a coin-flip, and the coin is why every projection you will see this week disagrees with the last one.

On the $700M opening and the $2.5-billion talk

Those numbers are real posts, but they trace to single X accounts (Portal Box Office, Beyond Reporter), not trade tracking. The trade consensus opening is ~$550M global, just under No Way Home. A $700M opening would be the second-biggest in history; nothing in the presales supports a number that far past NWH. And "bigger than Avengers: Doomsday" or "$2.5B" runs into simple math: No Way Home did $1.9B with the Maguire-Garfield event and without China. Brand New Day swaps one for the other. That nets out to No Way Home territory — a genuine $2B contender if China overperforms — not 30% above it.

What the internet is saying.

The ground readtrailers, presales, fan sentiment · late July
Running hot
Record presales
best first-day in 5 years · only NWH above
The final trailer's Hulk footage and the MJ-swinging beat drew the loudest reactions. Punisher's MCU entry is the fan-service the hardcore wanted. Director Cretton has framed Hulk and Punisher as thematic mirrors, not cameos — which has cooled the "stunt-casting" worry that trailed early news.
The caution
MCU fatigue?
2025 slate underwhelmed · the doubt in the room
The skeptics point at Fantastic Four, Brave New World and Thunderbolts all underdelivering in 2025. But Spider-Man has always been the MCU's most durable solo brand, and presales suggest the fatigue narrative doesn't apply to Peter Parker. The bet is that Spidey is fatigue-proof; the doubt is whether any MCU film is.

The mood splits clean down the middle. The presales say this is the biggest Spider-Man event since No Way Home. The skeptics say the wider MCU is wobbling after a rough 2025. Both are true at once. But here’s the thing worth remembering: Spider-Man has never once had a soft opening, in any era, under any studio. A fresh, alone-again Peter Parker walking in with the Hulk and the Punisher is about the strongest hand Marvel could be holding right now — and the audience clearly knows it.
